I’ve read a good few of the 1 to 3 star reviews on here and I want to express my feelings.
The food in the canteen is to notch and is the service/Staff please don’t listen to the absurd reviews of some of these people, where else in this city can you get enough pasta cooked in front of you and fresh for 2 meals for just $12?
Prime rib & 2 sides for $17 or Salmon and 2 sides for $14 both of which are cooked perfectly, it’s not a restaurant so stop complaining about well done medium rare and rare pieces just enjoy the meal and the fact you’re paying less then $20 for prime rib meal.
They have lots of choices for their proteins and sides.

I have been going here since the beginning and always have a wonderful experience.

The produce department always has has fresh and wonderful products available.

The meat section always has great deal and cuts and are always willing to cut what you need, the staff in meat and the seafood part are always great.

Grocery section has a great selection of everything and staff are friendly.

Bakery section are always in good shape and staff is friendly, I love their in store baked items.

The deli department is great with a wide selection of cheeses, my only issue is they need to learn how to cut sandwich meat properly on their slicer, but the staff is always friendly and helpful.

Overall this store is fantastic and has great prices only Loblaws store that has a fantastic Sunday sale which is great draw for the community.

I just felt I needed to say something after reading some of these negative comments from some people who obviously have to much time on their hands.

Great store and location and definitely stop in for their lunch program

text.text:
This is my favorite supermarket in the city, and it’s also my go-to spot for ready-to-eat meals. The place is spacious, and all the vegetables, fruits, and meats look incredibly fresh and neatly arranged. On weekends, there are often great deals. I usually get the sushi, pizza, sourdough bread, and the lunch entrees here. They have dishes like roasted beef, bbq pork ribs, and salmon —one entree with two side dishes for just $12, which is a very generous portion and usually takes me two meals to finish.
Today I was lucky to get some  wild-caught Argentina prawns on sale, and they also have lobster tails at a very reasonable price, which I love to buy as well. I also made a stop at the sourdough bread section. The sourdough here is much cheaper than other places, and I noticed they had two types of dark-colored Traditional Pumpernickel Bread Loaf, something I had never tried before. I asked an employee about all the ingredients, and she was very friendly and patiently explained them to me, so I decided to buy a loaf to try.
Of course, every time I come, I have to get the $12 salmon lunch with two sides. If you come at 11:00, the entrees are freshly baked, and they cook the salmon perfectly tender. This is my top recommendation. Besides that, there are always great discounts on fruits and vegetables during weekends, making it well worth the trip.

text.text:
This Costco location is very convenient, especially if you're staying downtown or around Chinatown. It's right next to the Stadium–Chinatown SkyTrain station, which makes it easy to get to without a car. The store has a wide selection of items—from fresh produce and household essentials to electronics, clothes, and pharmacy services.

The staff is generally helpful and the checkout lines move fairly quickly, although it can get crowded during weekends or late afternoons. The underground parking is useful, but it can be a bit tight and busy depending on the time of day.

One thing to note is the food court area. While the food is affordable and typical of Costco (hot dogs, pizza, chicken bakes, etc.), the eating area can be a bit disorganized. Tables are often not cleaned promptly, and it can be hard to find a place to sit, especially when it’s busy. The layout also makes the area feel a bit cramped.

Overall, it’s a good spot for bulk shopping in the heart of the city, but the dining area could use some better management.

My husband rarely gets a day off, so we came here for breakfast today. Their breakfast sandwiches and coffee are usually excellent — and the coffee today was just as good as always: rich, smooth, and fragrant.

However, the breakfast sandwich felt a little different this time. The egg portion was noticeably smaller than usual, which made the pesto mayo taste extra salty and tangy, throwing off the usual balance. Also, the placement of the Prosciutto Cotto really affects the flavor—fusion is great only when it improves on the original! 😄

Then again… it is the Monday after Sunday — we get it. Just making it to work on time is already an achievement 😝

Still love this place, and we’ll definitely be back. Fingers crossed the egg portion and flavor harmony return next time! 🥚✨

text.text:
I needed to stock up on tinned fish and pasta so I decided to include a visit to Bosa while running an errand not far away.

It was a warm and sunny winter sunday so I decided to walk from home downtown.  It was a loverly 1.5 hr walk along the Seawall and through revived neighbourhoods of Strathcona and Grandview-Woodlands.

After grabbing my provisions, I decided to pick up a drink and sandwich from the deli counter for lunch.  I did not take a picture of my sandwich but the grilled bacon and tomato panini could not be any more perfect with an orange pop for lunch in their sidewalk seating under the wintry sun.  The sandwich was piping hot coming out of the heater.  The breads were crispy and the thick bacon slices filled every bite.

text.text:
I visited this store today and picked up a single apple, which cost $0.77. When I got to the cashier, she asked, “Do you have cash?” I politely said I didn’t and apologized.

In response, the cashier let out a big sigh, shoved the card reader toward me without saying anything, and didn’t ask if I needed a receipt. Before I could even say “thank you, bye” she had already started ringing up the next customer, completely ignoring me.

I left feeling very disrespected and uncomfortable. I did nothing wrong—I simply didn’t have cash, but I was ready to pay. There was no reason to treat me like an inconvenience.

This kind of customer service is disappointing. Even for a small purchase, basic respect should always be shown.

text.text:
Windsor Meats is truly one of the local gems. After living in this neighborhood for 30+ years, I finally stopped by — and I’m so glad I did. I met Ian, introduced myself, and he made the entire experience exceptional. His attention to detail, politeness, and thoughtful recommendations were outstanding. The customer service was amazing.

I’m not sure whether he owns the place or works there, but he is incredibly welcoming — unlike my experiences at Columbus Meats on Nanaimo, where I often find the service rushed and unappreciative of customers. They rarely say “hello”; it’s usually just “what do you want?” Perhaps they take their business for granted.

I highly recommend Windsor Meats. Check them out and ask for Ian — he’s a great guy!

text.text:
Went hunting for beef brisket. Not super familiar with cuts of beef and definitely an amateur cook. Literally making my first ever slow cooker beef brisket dish. Anyway, shop was VERY clean and organized. The person at the counter was VERY nice. Willing to answer some of my amateur questions. The only area I was a tad disappointed by was not having a beef brisket that was grass-fed and grass-finished. Now, before any of you read me the riot act, I understand that some argue grain-finished has a better taste. I was also hoping for strictly pasture raised, but they did not know where it was or not. In the end, I bought four pounds. Next time, I'm going to search for a butcher where they know everything about the cattle they sell and where it comes from. This is personal preference so if that is not as important to you, I don't see any reason why you shouldn't give these folks a try.

I really enjoyed their customer service and I'll probably go back when in a pinch.
